endorsements.quote: Medical practitioners must be equipped with the skills to interpret AI outputs, recognise potential biases, and make informed decisions that prioritise patient safety.

Institutions should implement structured AI literacy programmes as part of medical training and continuing professional development, ensuring that clinicians remain at the forefront of technological advancements.
Liability and accountability: Clearly defining legal responsibility when AI-driven decisions lead to adverse patient outcomes.
Policymakers must ensure that AI implementation prioritises patient welfare over financial incentives, maintaining the human-centric nature of healthcare.
Bias mitigation: Policies to ensure AI models are trained on diverse, representative datasets to prevent discrimination.
Transparency must extend beyond patient interactions – health institutions and AI developers must openly disclose AI methodologies, performance metrics, and potential risks.

unlisted_practices: Establish an independent regulatory body to evaluate AI systems before deployment in clinical settings.
Strengthen data protection laws to ensure patient confidentiality and compliance with national healthcare data regulations.
Obtain informed consent from patients for AI use in diagnosis and treatment, including the ability to opt in or out of AI-assisted decision-making.
Educate patients and the public about AI-assisted medical decisions and communicate AI limitations and benefits transparently.
Have the National Department of Health establish ethical guidelines and governance structures for AI in healthcare.
Develop specific guidelines for AI-driven clinical decision support systems.
Centralise and integrate interoperable health records to support AI development.
Host health data and AI compute in-country through a national health data exchange and government cloud.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article discussing strategies, governance, and infrastructure recommendations for adopting AI in healthcare in South Africa.
